newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: SLOVAK GOVT, CBANK IN MONETARY POLICY TALKS - FINMIN.
newsitem.headline: SLOVAK GOVT, CBANK IN MONETARY POLICY TALKS - FINMIN.

text.p: Slovak Finance Minister Sergej Kozlik said on Thursday that the government was currently in talks with the central bank over "corrections" in monetary policy.

"We are, at present, in discussions with the central bank over some changes in its monetary policy," Kozlik said adding the topic was whether the central bank should ease its policies similar to the way the Czech Republic recently did.
Two weeks ago, the Czech central bank lowered its minimum reserve requirements for banks to 9.5 percent from a previous 11.5 percent.
"These are basic discussions at this time, no conclusions have come from the talks so far," he said.

The central bank (NBS) has gradually adopted measures designed to rein in a rapidly growing money supply since last summer, eventually creating a liqidity shortage on the interbak market at the beginning of the year, pushing interbank money rates to record levels of above 26 percent several times.

The high rates have sparked criticism from the industrial sector, banks and even the finance ministry, all of whom have called for policy loosening to ensure cheaper funds for further restructuring of the badly-undercapitalised Slovak economy.
The NBS, however, said on April 11 that it may not further ease monetary policy since this would make it difficult to keep inflation -- at 6.3 percent, year-on-year, in March -- under control.
